Limitations: This is a headless native form-host feasibility probe, not a production form editor or an Avalonia IME implementation.
Full static TrueType font with BMP identity CID coverage; supplementary Unicode, shaping, vertical writing, CFF and TTC are not covered.

Native form input commits correct canonical values but regenerates CJK appearance with unembedded system-font fallback. A bounded managed appearance bridge is required after every commit; native automatic font compatibility is rejected.

The managed bridge supports this fixture's fixed size, left aligned single line, explicit newline text and fully visible single-choice list only. Auto wrapping, scrolling, rotation, text fitting and arbitrary existing form layouts are not implemented.
A value-only annotation subset is insufficient for arbitrary later input; the full licensed font is retained in AcroForm default resources.
Independent pypdf canonical field, default-resource and appearance checks plus Poppler rendering are required.

observations: All six complete saved/reedited final pages were individually inspected after the final unified run. Latin baseline text and field borders remain clear.
LXGW Chinese, Zen Japanese/Traditional Han, and Gowun precomposed Hangul render distinct readable glyphs with no missing-glyph squares, overlap, or clipping in final bridged outputs.

Both explicit multiline rows are visible with adequate spacing. The first save selects the second list row; reedited outputs select the third ABC row with blue background and white glyphs. All other list rows remain visible.

Gowun native reedited counterexample was individually inspected: canonical Hangul values survive, but displayed Hangul is replaced by missing-glyph squares. That raw PDF is evidence of rejected native fallback, never a passing output.

Three input pages and the other raw native pages were not individually inspected during this final review; only hashes/independent checks bind those images, with inputs additionally visible in the inspected overview.
